candidate_relations.reason: The biopsy results explicitly confirm VTC (vesicular thyroid carcinoma, i.e., follicular thyroid carcinoma) metastasis at both the costal and sinonasal sites. Papillary thyroid carcinoma is a different histological subtype. While C001 correctly captures the low iodine avidity/radioiodine-refractory aspect and the presence of metastasis, it asserts an incompatible subtype (papillary vs. vesicular/follicular). The reference diagnosis specifically requires VTC with sinonasal metastasis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Papillary thyroid carcinoma is a distinct histological subtype incompatible with vesicular (follicular) thyroid carcinoma; both are differentiated thyroid carcinomas but represent different subtypes with different metastatic patterns and molecular profiles

case_quality_flags: VTC likely refers to follicular (vesicular) thyroid carcinoma; hematogenous spread to ribs and vertebrae is characteristic of follicular rather than papillary thyroid carcinoma, supporting the biopsy-confirmed diagnosis
Sinonasal metastasis from thyroid carcinoma is rare; the radioiodine-refractory designation is supported by low uptake in the sinonasal tumor on scintigraphy
